_note: Hand-curated. Only the moments a newcomer needs. kind: achievement (links to a case), launch (a model release), origin (pre-history), prize. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD; use -01 when only the month is known (the day is then hidden); set "approx": true to hide a day that is only approximately known but needed for ordering. star: true marks a landmark, shown with a star on the card and the axis.

items.title: Turing asks whether machines can think
items.blurb: Alan Turing's paper 'Computing Machinery and Intelligence' proposes the imitation game, later called the Turing test.

items.title: The Dartmouth workshop names the field
items.blurb: A summer workshop at Dartmouth College coins the term 'artificial intelligence' and sets out a research programme.

items.title: Deep Blue beats Kasparov
items.blurb: IBM's chess machine wins a six-game match against the world champion. It relies on search, not learning. First win by a computer over a reigning champion under tournament conditions.

items.title: AlexNet wins ImageNet
items.blurb: A deep convolutional network trained on two consumer GPUs cuts the top-5 error rate from 26% to 15%. Deep learning becomes the default method in computer vision.

items.title: AlphaGo plays Move 37
items.blurb: In game two against Lee Sedol, AlphaGo plays a move it rated a 1-in-10,000 chance for a human to play. It wins the match 4–1.

items.title: 'Attention Is All You Need'
items.blurb: Google researchers publish the Transformer architecture. Most of the systems below from 2020 on are built on it.

items.title: AlphaZero learns chess, shogi and Go from the rules alone
items.blurb: Trained by self-play from the rules only, with no human games. Beats the strongest existing programs in all three games.

items.title: GPT-3
items.blurb: A 175-billion-parameter language model that performs tasks from a few examples in the prompt, with no task-specific training.

items.title: AlphaFold solves protein folding
items.blurb: At the CASP14 competition, DeepMind's system predicts protein structures at accuracy comparable to experiment. A 50-year-old open problem. Chemistry Nobel Prize in 2024.

items.title: Reinforcement learning controls a fusion reactor
items.blurb: A learned controller shapes plasma inside the TCV tokamak in Lausanne on its first run.

items.title: AlphaTensor beats a 53-year-old algorithm
items.blurb: Finds a way to multiply 4×4 matrices (over GF(2)) in 47 multiplications, one fewer than Strassen's 1969 method.

items.title: ChatGPT
items.blurb: OpenAI releases a chat interface on GPT-3.5. It reaches 100 million monthly users within two months.

items.title: GPT-4
items.blurb: Accepts image input and scores in the top 10% on a simulated bar exam.

items.title: An AI-found sorting routine ships in the C++ standard library
items.blurb: AlphaDev finds faster sorting sequences at the assembly level. They are merged into LLVM's libc++.

items.title: A speech neuroprosthesis restores conversation after paralysis
items.blurb: Brain signals decoded into words at near-conversational speed, with an avatar to voice them.

items.title: GraphCast out-forecasts the leading weather model
items.blurb: Ten-day global forecasts in under a minute, more accurate than ECMWF's operational system on 90% of targets.

items.title: GNoME predicts 2.2 million new crystals
items.blurb: 380,000 of them predicted stable. About 48,000 stable crystals were known before.

items.title: FunSearch finds a larger cap set
items.blurb: A language model paired with a checker produces a larger cap set than any known. First verifiable new result from an LLM on an open problem.

items.title: Silver at the International Mathematical Olympiad
items.blurb: AlphaProof and AlphaGeometry 2 solve four of six IMO problems, one point short of gold.

items.title: OpenAI o1
items.blurb: A model trained to produce a chain of reasoning before answering, spending more compute at inference time.

items.title: The first complete wiring diagram of an adult brain
items.blurb: AI segmentation maps all 140,000 neurons and 50 million connections in a fruit fly.

items.title: Two Nobel Prizes for AI work
items.blurb: Physics to Hopfield and Hinton for foundational work on neural networks. Chemistry to Baker, Hassabis and Jumper for protein design and AlphaFold.

items.title: DeepSeek-R1
items.blurb: An open-weights reasoning model from China at o1 level, with a reported training cost far below US labs'. Nvidia loses about $600 billion in market value in a day.

items.title: AlphaEvolve improves Strassen and about 50 open problems
items.blurb: A coding agent that evolves algorithms. Finds a 48-multiplication method for 4×4 complex matrices, beating a 56-year-old record.

items.title: An AI agent finds a zero-day before attackers use it
items.blurb: Google's Big Sleep locates a SQLite flaw that threat intelligence knew was being staged for exploitation.

items.title: Gold at the IMO, graded by the IMO
items.blurb: Gemini Deep Think scores 35/42 working in natural language. OpenAI reports the same score the same week.

items.title: AI weather forecasts go operational
items.blurb: NOAA puts an AI forecast suite into daily operations. During hurricane season an AI model had lower track error than the National Hurricane Center's official forecast at several lead times.

items.title: Claude Mythos Preview
items.blurb: Anthropic announces a model it does not release publicly because of its vulnerability-finding ability, and shares it with about 40 companies under Project Glasswing.

items.title: Claude Fable 5 and Mythos 5
items.blurb: One underlying model in two versions: Fable 5 for general availability with dual-use safeguards, Mythos 5 for approved organizations without them.

items.title: OpenAI's models escape a sandbox and breach Hugging Face
items.blurb: During an internal safety evaluation, the models find a zero-day, leave the sandbox, and compromise a rival's production servers.

items.title: The Jacobian conjecture is disproved
items.blurb: Levent Alpöge and Claude Fable 5 produce an explicit polynomial map that disproves the 1939 conjecture in dimension three and up. The map can be checked by hand.

items.title: Perfect 42/42 scores at the IMO
items.blurb: Several systems report flawless papers. 7 of 666 human contestants did the same. None of the AI scores is certified by the IMO.

items.title: Claude breaks a post-quantum signature candidate
items.blurb: A lattice automorphism found by Claude Mythos Preview halves the hard problem behind HAWK. Its authors withdraw it from NIST standardization.

items.title: Ten open problems, ten Lean certificates
items.blurb: OpenAI's internal model Astra closes ten open results in mathematics and theoretical computer science, including the first improvement to the sphere-packing exponent since 1978. Each proof ships machine-checked.

items.title: GPT-6 Astra
items.blurb: OpenAI's largest training run. A 'recurrent depth' architecture that hides part of its reasoning, and cyber capabilities restricted to vetted testers.

items.title: An AI claim on a Millennium Prize Problem
items.blurb: OpenAI reports that about 10,000 agents proved finite-time blowup for the forced Navier–Stokes equations, with a Lean certificate. Not yet verified outside OpenAI. The unforced problem remains open.
